questions.short: Nightly positions map red: topic naming
questions.question: Why do topic-name calls through the Codex CLI fail (149 of 867 topics on 2026-10-26, 555 of 988 on 2026-10-25, 442 of 844 on 2026-10-22), and why does the naming step take hours (18,690 s on 2026-10-26)?
questions.blocks: whether the nightly session import and positions map stay green, which is how the brian-positions skill stays current (the next plan)
questions.resolves_with: Running settles the first part, not an evaluation: reproduce one failing call with the full Codex CLI stderr (the concern keeps only its first line). Reading settled why failures repeat: a failed topic is never written to the names file (tools/name_topics.py:79-87), the nightly run deletes the names file before naming (tools/nightly_sessions.py:81) and only names that were written carry over (tools/name_topics.py:51), so every topic that failed once is retried every night until a call succeeds. 867 is the number of topics in the build, not the number of calls; the nightly log does not record how many were carried. See docs/planning/next-plan.md step 1.

questions.question: extract-or-run.service restarts every few seconds (NRestarts 2537 on 2026-10-27) because it is the older invocation of tools/extract_queue.py over private/extract_full_20261003/or_run with --budget 25 and no --contract. tools/finish_pipeline.sh:15 already reruns the same queue with --contract docs/capture_contracts/extraction-position-memory.json and INQUIRY_EXTRACT_MOVES=1, but it first waits for every extract-* unit to stop (tools/finish_pipeline.sh:12), so the looping unit also holds the finish pipeline back. Is anything in that queue unfinished?
questions.blocks: how issue #191 closes, and whether the full-archive extraction resumes
questions.resolves_with: Prior art settles the remedy: the contract and the contract-bearing invocation exist. Disable the unit; reading the queue's output folder settles whether anything is unfinished, and if so finish_pipeline.sh (or its line 15 alone) runs it. See docs/planning/next-plan.md step 2.

questions.short: Backfill moves for the 2,176 existing graphs?
questions.question: Should the 2,176 archive graphs extracted before 2026-10-06 be re-extracted to add moves (how Brian argues)? New runs already capture moves: the adopted capture contract decided to (docs/capture_contracts/extraction-position-memory.json, fields.moves) and tools/finish_pipeline.sh:15 sets INQUIRY_EXTRACT_MOVES=1. The old graphs still have 0 moves.
questions.blocks: any use of reasoning motifs or move sequences across the whole archive (tools/mine_motifs.py works only on the hand-built fixtures today)
questions.resolves_with: Prior art settles the method, not the call: the capture-contract rule (docs/design/capture-contract.md:11) compares capture cost with the chance of later need, and the contract's own note prices the backfill at about $8.5 (a full re-run, C*(1+f)) and says it needs Brian's decision. No test is needed.
questions.recommendation: Approve the backfill when the next full re-extraction runs for another reason, so moves ride along at no extra run; do not schedule a separate $8.5 run today, since no consumer reads archive moves yet.
questions.default: New runs keep capturing moves; the 2,176 older graphs stay without them until a full re-extraction happens.

questions.question: Should the five-condition terminal-state reader benchmark (issue #225: does the corrected extractor improve an independent reader's resumption accuracy on the 2026-10-18 conversation) be run with live models?
questions.blocks: whether the 2026-10-18 extractor task and status corrections are judged by reader accuracy, and whether any schema change is considered for resumption
questions.resolves_with: Prior art and argument first: the roadmap forbids another benchmark without explicit approval, and the harness's own README says a schema change is considered only if existing elements cannot encode the terminal state, which the deterministic part already showed they can. A run would change one decision, whether to keep investing in resumption from graphs versus reading the raw tail; it is a single conversation, so it cannot generalize.
questions.recommendation: Do not run it now; the deterministic result already settles the schema question, and a one-conversation reader score would not change the roadmap.
questions.default: Issue #225 stays open and unrun; PR #218's protocol stays unmerged until someone needs it.

questions.short: Does the code execute typed rules?
questions.question: Does Inquiry Graph evaluate typed rules, so that its system model needs a metamodel mapped onto the shared kernel?
questions.blocks: system_model.executes_typed_rules and whether a metamodel is owed
questions.resolves_with: Reading the code and the metamodel reference settled it.
questions.evidence: No. Relations have named roles, but SIGNATURES only constrains which node kinds each role may bind and validate() checks shape (src/inquiry_graph/validate.py:67-82); no relation carries a formula, condition or effect that is evaluated, which is the trigger in bounded-design's typed-relational-metamodels reference. A kernel crosswalk exists as PR #15, kept unmerged on purpose.
